classification_contract.a1_interpretation: The seventeen normalized implementation-role nouns in the PGIR-002 objective; no separate A1 appendix or JSON Schema exists in the frozen source.
classification_contract.method: Behavior-first static inspection of source, registry declarations, importability, and focused tests at the bound authority tree.
classification_contract.module_record_rule: Every module record names one existing repository-relative path, exactly one disposition, and one or more evidence paths. A canonical disposition is scoped to the exact interface stated by authority_scope; it is not a repository-wide promotion claim.
classification_contract.role_coverage_rule: Every A1 role occurs exactly once in role_coverage with one scalar disposition and nonempty evidence_paths. Existing components can coexist with an unresolved repository-wide owner.
classification_contract.unresolved_rule: An unresolved record has module_path null and records the observed components and evidence; no missing module is fabricated.
classification_contract.sorting: modules are bytewise ascending by path; IDs and evidence paths are bytewise unique within their arrays

disposition_definitions.canonical: The sole owner selected for the exact named interface and authority scope.
disposition_definitions.component: An active subordinate or family-specific implementation that does not own the repository-wide role.
disposition_definitions.generated: A materialized derivative that cannot own source semantics.
disposition_definitions.facade: An import or API delegation surface whose semantics are owned elsewhere.
disposition_definitions.legacy: A supported prior or compatibility meaning that is not promotion authority.
disposition_definitions.experimental: A bounded candidate, research, or advisory implementation that is not semantic or proof authority.
disposition_definitions.artifact: A data, schema, policy, or checkpoint object rather than an executable semantic owner.
disposition_definitions.declaration: A protocol, metadata, registry, or data-boundary declaration with no operational ownership claim.
disposition_definitions.duplicate: A redundant compatibility implementation or re-export with an identified owner elsewhere.
disposition_definitions.obsolete: An explicitly deprecated or replaced surface.
disposition_definitions.unresolved: No single live implementation owns the stated scope at the bound authority tree.

roles.decision: Shared authority/result contracts and domain IR owners are explicit; no claim is made that distinct formula-family ASTs are interchangeable.
Parsing is family-specific. The deterministic deontic and TDFOL parsers are scoped owners, not a repository-wide parser substitute.
The domain-neutral layer owns immutable artifacts, protocols, views, and guards; operational family lowering remains in adapters.
Six registered adapters and a legacy bridge envelope exist, but no single rich typed repository-wide bridge owns their semantics.
COMPILER-CURRENT-1 is the deterministic measured Legal compiler plus registered typed family adapters; declaration protocols and parallel family compilers do not replace it.
DECOMPILER-CURRENT-1 uses the source-withheld Legal owner and controlled family decoders; there is no domain-neutral formalization decompiler.
Shared canonical JSON and identity primitives own encoding; the Intent helper is a domain projection onto that class of behavior.
The typed source-map ledger and CanonicalRoundTripIR SourceMapEntry contract preserve source grounding and cross-reference integrity.
Proof authority is typed and fail-closed, while proving remains a bounded family/backend portfolio; no component may substitute result authority.
Countermodel extraction exists for the TDFOL family and is not represented as a cross-family proof result.
Canonical component/source-map traces coexist with a timestamp-bearing legacy optimizer proof trace; the latter is not content identity.
The external prover router is a bounded execution component; Leanstral only proposes candidates and is explicitly nonauthoritative.
Embeddings and numeric features are source-bound inputs to retrieval or advice, never semantic or proof authority.
CID-keyed FAISS vectors are verified retrieval artifacts whose hits are context-only and never proof authority.
Many family metrics and experimental objectives exist, but no fixed repository-wide IRLossConfiguration@1 owns their signs, normalization, and authority exclusions.
Advisor compatibility metadata, modal numeric state, and the external legacy model are three noninterchangeable checkpoint meanings; none is a unified semantic checkpoint owner.
Packaging and approval-gated publishing components exist, but no publication owner binds compiler, loss, proof, evaluation, promotion, and rollback identities required for PGIR release authority.

explicit_nonclaims: The reviewed comparison commit is comparison-only and is not substituted for SRC-DATASETS-AUTH-1.
A canonical module classification is limited to its authority_scope and does not make every similarly named class interchangeable.
FormalizationCompiler is a structural protocol and artifact boundary, not a second COMPILER-CURRENT-1 implementation.
ProofObligation and evidence declarations are not proof results, and no adapter may substitute result authority.
Bridge LegalIRDocument and canonical Legal CanonicalRoundTripIR are parallel envelopes, not aliases.
TDFOL, DCEC, Intent, Security, Legal, and optimizer ModalIR retain distinct family identity; there is no repository-wide Formula type.
Advisor, Leanstral, autoencoder, embedding, vector, and loss outputs are candidate, retrieval, or training signals and never semantic or proof authority.
MODEL-LEGACY-1 is artifact-only and never training or promotion authority.
The focused tests establish the stated structural and authority contracts; they do not prove semantic completeness for every logic family.
No comparison-only module absent from the authority tree is represented as a live implementation.
No DomainLogicSlice implementation exists at this authority tree; this inventory does not invent one.
